# Figure captions (generated by make_figures.py)

Fig. 1. Monthly share of unreliable decision forecasts (|f(w_t) − p̄_t| > AUD 300/MWh) across the five NEM regions. Shading marks the fit (72,865 intervals), validation (14,640), test (14,650) and 2023–25 replication (261,635) periods. October 2022 is excluded because the AEMO archive holds only the latest pre-dispatch run for that month.

Fig. 3. Information timeline for one trading interval. Features use only pre-dispatch runs published up to the decision run (shaded). The label compares the decision forecast f(w_t) with the mean of the six settled 5-min DISPATCHPRICE values (INTERVENTION = 0): Y_t = 1[|f(w_t) − p̄_t| > δ_Y], δ_Y = AUD 300/MWh. Run spacing is schematic.

Fig. 4. Mean absolute error of the decision forecast against the settled price in extreme and normal intervals, 2023–25 (R1; log scale). Labels give the ratio of means (28–56); Welch p < 0.001 in every region.

Fig. 5. ROC (a) and precision–recall (b) curves of the FRI model, fitted on 2021–22 and frozen, on the 2022 test set (14,650 intervals, 94 unreliable) and the 2023–25 replication (261,635 intervals). The dash-dot curve is raw recent_std_3h on 2023–25 (R4 comparison).

Fig. 6. Feature importance of the FRI model (17 features). The decision forecast accounts for 44.2% and the revision-path group for 37.1%.

Fig. 7. Energy discharged into over-forecast intervals (f(w_t) − p̄_t > AUD 300/MWh) by agent, β = 2.03. FRI reduces exposure against the baseline by 68.5% in 2022 (95% CI [0.0, 100.8] MWh) and by 47.0% in 2023–25 (vol - FRI 557.6 MWh [387.7, 744.6]; R3).

Fig. 8. Net revenue of the baseline, FRI and constant ×0.25 agents as degradation becomes less convex (R6). α is rescaled at each β so that baseline degradation cost is unchanged. The constant ×0.25 advantage at β = 2.03 disappears at β = 1.0 in both periods.

Fig. 9. AUC by region for the frozen FRI model (exploratory). n+ gives the number of unreliable intervals (2023–25; 2022 test). The dashed line is the pooled 2023–25 AUC (R2).
